messages:
Anna Li: Heads up — after today's NF4 rollout run on prod-like nightlies we hit a repeatable regression: ~30% throughput drop + memory spike on 32xA10 cluster. Noticed around the 2nd warmup batch.
Mike Torres: Do you have the job id / logs? was this new kernel selection or fallback path? :thinking:
Anna Li: job id: run/2026-02-22/nf4-nightly-17
perf-bot: Regression alert: job run/2026-02-22/nf4-nightly-17 — p50 throughput -29%, p95 latency +18%, GPU mem +14% (compared to baseline 176k). Link: https://perf.internal/runs/1782345678
Anna Li: Quick paste of the main stacktrace (truncated):
```
[2026-02-22 03:12:41] kernel_select: chosen=fp4_kv_split (fallback), reason=quant_scale_mismatch
[2026-02-22 03:12:41] batching: flush_threshold hit, batch_size=16, tokens=2048
[2026-02-22 03:12:42] kv_cache: alloc failed try_coalesce -> new_segment=256MB, total_kv_segments=48
```
Julia Park: Interesting — fallback to fp4_kv_split. That path's kernels are older and don't use the new continuous-batching fast path. Did calibration change per-layer scales? We ran a large calib sweep last night.
Samir Patel: I repro'd locally with the nightly model build (sha: a3f5e2). Repro commands:
```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python tests/bench_infer.py --model nf4-v1 --batcher.max_tokens=2000 --use_kv_cache=1 --calib-run=nightly
```
Samir Patel: With the above I saw kv segment churn spikes and allocator fragmentation. nvprof shows repeated cudaMalloc calls around attention kernels.
Mike Torres: Can you paste the nvprof snippet? Also, what's the difference in quant params between baseline vs candidate?
Samir Patel: nvprof snippet:
```
malloc 0.5s cudaMemcpy 0.2s aten::conv 0.8s fp4_kv_split::forward 1.2s
```
Samir Patel: Baseline (stable) quant scales: per-tensor per-layer median ~ 0.023. Candidate (post-calib) had more variance + per-head skew -> some layers flagged use_nf4_opt=false which forces fp4_kv_split.
Anna Li: The batching heuristic also kicked: when batcher.max_tokens >= 1800 we hit the slow path more often because we ended up with long prefix reuse that the fp4_kv_split kernel doesn't recycle efficiently.
Julia Park: So two interacting things: calibration produced scale variance -> kernel selector picks slower kernel; long token batches + KV reuse -> allocator churn + fragmentation -> memory spike and fallback to smaller segments -> throughput drops.
Mike Torres: Proposed short-term mitigations:
- revert last night's calib sweep for stable
- force kernel selector to prefer nf4_fast when compatible (override flag)
- reduce batcher.max_tokens to 1400 for canaries
Samir Patel: I added a temporary guard in runtime: if selected_kernel==fp4_kv_split and batcher.max_tokens>1600 -> force nf4_fast (if compatibility check passes). Quick patch: `if (kernel == FP4_KV_SPLIT && batcher.max_tokens > 1600) kernel = NF4_FAST;`
Anna Li: Can we run a focused perf job that toggles only the kernel selector (keep calib changes) to prove causality?
perf-bot: New perf job queued: /runs/1782345801 — A/B: kernel-selector-override ON/OFF, 1000 samples
Julia Park: Also want a deep profile of allocator behavior. Suggested tools: nsight-memcheck + our custom kv-alloc-telemetry. Example command:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=run_kv.nsys \ 
  --capture-range=nvtx -- python infra/bench/kvcache_profile.py --samples=500
```
Samir Patel: Ran that. Key findings:
- free list fragmentation increased after calib (avg free-block-size down 35%)
- repeated small cudaMallocs every 20ms coinciding with kv evictions
- total number of segments increased by 3x compared to baseline
Mike Torres: Long-term we should make kernel selection aware of allocator pressure and batching heuristics (score = perf_estimate - alloc_cost). Also consider adding a compact-on-demand step to merge KV segments.
Anna Li: OK immediate plan agreed:
1) rollback calib sweep for stable channel (ops action)
2) deploy kernel-selector override to canaries + reduce batcher.max_tokens to 1400 for canary cluster
3) run perf-bot A/B and memprofile job (priority)
4) design follow-up: allocator compaction + kernel selector cost model
infra-bot: Rolling change: calib-sweep revert queued (change-id: CHG-2026-0421). Canaries will start in 10m.
Mike Torres: I'll own the kernel-selector override PR. Samir — can you attach the nvprof/nsys output to the perf ticket?
Samir Patel: Yep uploading to https://perf.internal/artifacts/1782345678
Julia Park: Leaving a note: this was subtle because end-to-end evals didn't hit the long-prefix distribution; only our large-batcher nightlies did. Add distribution tests to catch this.
Anna Li: Thanks team — let's sync tomorrow 10am if A/B shows anything. :coffee:
perf-bot: Regression job /runs/1782345801 scheduled. We'll post results when ready.
